Breaking: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5184 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning.
  • In a recent development, the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image.
  • In a recent development, all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

In a recent development, the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A latest midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

In a recent development, all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

According to recent reports, “It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca stated, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

Industry observers note that his team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Industry observers note that momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

Marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

It has been revealed that his team revealed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, fresh signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

According to recent reports, they could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his latest manager.

It has been revealed that "That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a massive ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “upcoming Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a upcoming season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2.

The Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

Sources indicate that maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

Sources indicate that guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the fresh Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

According to recent reports, bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

Sources indicate that jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

Foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

Ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

In a recent development, guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

Industry observers note that bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

Recent findings suggest that chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

Industry observers note that villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

City are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

Little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

Anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

It has been revealed that dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

According to recent reports, nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Shows how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

Brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

In a recent development, you’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

Industry observers note that de Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Sources indicate that villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

We’re back under way at the Amex.

Boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four massive summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

Industry observers note that there’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

A nightmare start for Emery’s side.

Sources indicate that there’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

City now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to blueprint when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

According to recent reports, CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

Recent findings suggest that ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

Moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

According to recent reports, VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Industry observers note that some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

According to recent reports, A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

This is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

Manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

City have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

Villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

Industry observers note that bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

Sources indicate that the second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

In a recent development, brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

Recent findings suggest that chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

Gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

Brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

It has been revealed that lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

City have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his new bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

Chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

In a recent development, villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

That’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”.

Sources indicate that after being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”.

"Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA.

Recent findings suggest that on taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s major emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”.

When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

In a recent development, “We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a substantial player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”.

In a recent development, brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Sources indicate that pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he stated of Guardiola’s grand design.

In a recent development, tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

The Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for new signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Representing Aston Villa 👊 pic.twitter.com/JjqgYhBzwb.

According to recent reports, TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Here's how we start 🆚 Villa! 👊 pic.twitter.com/nnFj5swsdg.

It has been revealed that some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be stated for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some new midfielders in the coming weeks.

Recent findings suggest that welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a fresh era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut….

It has been revealed that the Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

In a recent development, brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

    • Week 12 of the NFL season kicked off with a rare Wednesday matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, prepping us for a full Thanksgiving feast of football the following day, headlined by an MVP showcase between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday night.
    • Ahead of that matchup, the Steelers made headlines by reportedly benching veteran quarterback and former MVP Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph for Week 12 after recent struggles on offense.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Week 12 of the NFL season kicked off with a rare Wednesday matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, prepping us for a full Thanksgiving feast of football the following day, headlined by an MVP showcase between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday night.

    Ahead of that matchup, the Steelers made headlines by reportedly benching veteran quarterback and former MVP Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph for Week 12 after recent struggles on offense.

    This storyline then reached a fever pitch on Wednesday when Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" and went scorched-earth on a rant about head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers accused McCarthy of repeatedly falling asleep in meetings and ending a team breakdown with "1-2-3 Let's go Packers.".

    Sources indicate that shortly after his appearance on the show, the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac reported that Rodgers was being released. The quarterback had said on the show that he was "not going back to Pittsburgh." He was officially waived on Wednesday afternoon's transaction wire.

    We're watching plenty of injuries ahead of the action, including Las Vegas Raiders All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers, who missed Week 11 with an ankle injury, though he was reportedly pushing to play in that matchup. The Kansas City Chiefs have already ruled out running back Kenneth Walker III for his third consecutive game with a groin injury, giving rookie Emmett Johnson the nod for a Thanksgiving contest with the Buffalo Bills.

    Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 11.

    Recent findings suggest that 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy did not practice on Thursday. It was his second straight day without practicing as he deals with an ankle injury. If he can't play on Sunday, it would be backup quarterback Mac Jones taking over against the Seahawks.

    Veteran wide receiver Mike Evans was upgraded to a limited practice participant after not practicing on Wednesday.

    The rookie quarterback continues to deal with a back injury and missed his second consecutive practice of the week.

    If Beck misses Sunday's game, Josh Johnson is projected to be under center against the Commanders. Arizona did bring back Kedon Slovis this week after he was waived by the Ravens, but there hasn't been any indication that head coach Mike LaFleur is leaning toward starting Slovis after claiming him this week.

    Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert remains in the league's concussion protocol and missed practice on Thursday.

    If he doesn't practice on Friday, he will likely miss L.A.'s game on Sunday against the Patriots in which backup quarterback DJ Uiagalelei will likely be under center.

    The Jaguars' offense had some concerning entries on the injury report on Thursday.

    Wide receiver Parker Washington was limited due to a shoulder problem after not being on the injury report on Wednesday.

    Starting running back Bhayshul Tuten missed his second consecutive day of practice due to an ankle and foot injury.

    Jacksonville will have one more day of practice on Friday before statuses for Sunday's game against Tennessee are due.

    Industry observers note that the Steelers have had a tumultuous week, but got at least a spot of good news on Thanksgiving as veteran wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. was activated off of IR.

    Pittman is expected to play for Pittsburgh against the Broncos on Friday afternoon.

    The veteran wideout was acquired from the Colts ahead of the regular season and promptly agreed to a 3-year, $59 million extension.

    Recent findings suggest that pittman has played in only three games this season and has been on IR since October 10 due to a left foot injury. He heads into this week's game with 89 yards on seven receptions and is still looking for his first touchdown as a Steeler.

    It's a real shame the sports world learned about Mike McCarthy's ice cream sandwich assistant after Halloween. Given the absurdity of that revelation, the Pittsburgh Steelers coach's ice cream pal would have been a popular costume among sports fans looking to have fun with the moment.

    Recent findings suggest that thankfully, McCarthy's ice cream sandwich assistant is also perfectly in theme for the next major holiday. Thanksgiving is here in the United States, and, as you might have guessed, McCarthy's ice cream assistant is getting a little extra attention as fans and sports stars get ready to sit down for a day of gluttonous behavior.

    According to recent reports, houston Rockets star Kevin Durant was among the biggest names to reference McCarthy's ice cream sandwich assistant on Thanksgiving. Durant called the move a "great idea," and said he would be hiring an ice cream assistant of his own on the holiday.

    If you somehow missed the whole McCarthy saga, well, here's a refresher. After learning he was being benched by the Steelers, quarterback Aaron Rodgers went on Pat McAfee's show and completely blasted his own head coach.

    According to recent reports, rodgers said, frankly, a lot of wild things. He claimed McCarthy fell asleep in team meetings regularly and broke down the Steelers with a chant of "1-2-3 Packers" during their last game. Some of those claims have been confirmed by local media or McCarthy himself.

    But the ice cream sandwich assistant has even shadier origins. As all the Rodgers madness was popping off, former Steelers DT Breiden Fehoko claimed McCarthy had an ice cream sandwich assistant, someone responsible for bringing the coach an ice cream sandwich on demand. Fehoko claimed he received that information from a Steelers player.

    That report has not been confirmed by local reporters or McCarthy himself, though that's not going to stop sports fans from having a little fun.

    Recent findings suggest that 1. Upcoming York Jets (Trade with Tennessee Titans) — Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State.

    In this deal, the Jets keep the No. 5 overall pick and package the Nos. 4 and 15 picks and a 2028 second-rounder to move up and tab Mestemaker as their QB of the future. Mestemaker has solid size (6-foot-3, 215 pounds) with a good but not overwhelming arm. He plays in a friendly offense that he maximizes with his aggressiveness. He's a loose athlete with a knack for changing arm slots and the arc on his throws. He's had some inconsistent play over the last month or so as his aggression leads to too many dicey decisions. Yet he's the exact type of gunslinger who would be fun to pair with the Jets' assortment of talented young skill players.

    According to recent reports, 2. Los Angeles Chargers — Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State.

    A season from hell can have its rewards!

    Three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald said what the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams might all be thinking: "I wish he would stay out one more week.".

    Recent findings suggest that donald was referring to Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons. A member of the Packers might also have applied the sentiment to Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett.

    Instead, the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game will feature a matchup of two teams who spent big to upgrade their pass rush recently — before injuries sunk their hopes within months.

    The Jaguars were without running back Bhayshul Tuten at Wednesday's practice as he deals with both a foot and ankle injury.

    With the chaotic week, Jacksonville benefits from a normal schedule, not having to play the Titans until Sunday.

    Recent findings suggest that tuten has played in all 10 games for Jacksonville this season. He has 642 yards and five touchdowns on 158 carries, and has added an additional 226 yards and three more scores on 21 receptions.

    San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is dealing with an ankle injury, head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Wednesday.

    Shanahan specified that Purdy does not have a high-ankle injury, but the quarterback may not be able to play Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks.

    If Purdy can't start the NFC West divisional game, backup quarterback Mac Jones is expected to take over.

    San Francisco is 9-1 and leads both the division and the NFC. The 49ers had their bye week in Week 8 and have won three consecutive games.

    According to recent reports, purdy is having one of the best seasons of his career. In just 10 games, he has already thrown more touchdowns (23) than in each of his last two seasons (20). Purdy has thrown for 2,624 yards and five interceptions, and has added 222 additional yards and two more scores on the ground.

    While the Rams continue taking injury hits on offense, they are getting a reinforcement on defense.

    Defensive end Kobie Turner has been activated ahead of Wednesday night's game against the Packers.

    Recent findings suggest that turner had been on IR because of a groin injury and last played on October 18. He heads into tonight's game with just seven sacks on the year.

    The Steelers have reportedly released veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers, per Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac.

    Rodgers' release was reportedly expedited after the quarterback went scorched-earth on former head coach Mike McCarthy on Wednesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show.".

    The NFL went out of its way to schedule five compelling matchups for Thanksgiving Eve, Thanksgiving and Black Friday.

    The schedule comes out in May, and things can change dramatically over six months. Yet four of the five matchups have held up very well. That's not a bad percentage, even if the Eagles and Cowboys have let us down. Everyone will watch those two marquee franchises anyway.

    There's a lot on the line in terms of the playoff race during this week. We rank the most important games, in terms of what's at stake.

    Veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has signed with the Washington Commanders practice squad as a free agent, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday.

    According to recent reports, aiyuk was released by the 49ers on Monday and passed through waivers on Tuesday, going unclaimed. Now, he reunites with his former teammate at Arizona State, quarterback Jayden Daniels.

    The Commanders, fresh off a stunning upset over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 11, have been in need of help at receiver following a season-ending injury to star wideout Terry McLaurin. The team sits at 4-5-1, just two games back from the Fresh York Giants, who hold the lead in the NFC East.

    This marks a fresh start for the 28-year-old, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract extension with the 49ers ahead of the 2024 season but played just seven games on the new deal. He tore his ACL and MCL on Oct. 20, 2024, ending his season.

    Read more on Aiyuk's recent signing.

    Recent findings suggest that the Chiefs are looking at another game without star running back Kenneth Walker III. Despite returning to practice Tuesday, Walker will reportedly not play against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving, according to multiple reports.

    It will mark the third straight game Walker will miss due to the problem.

    Prior to the injury, Walker was well on his way toward posting his finest season in the NFL. Through eight games, the running back already rushed for 872 yards and seven touchdowns. He also hauled in 26 catches for 172 yards and four receiving scores.

    There were four MVPs, 10 Pro Bowls, a Super Bowl championship, dozens of highlights that defied belief over 22 seasons, and it all seems to end with a quick statement from the team after most of Pittsburgh had already gone to sleep.

    In a recent development, it's not like Rodgers has played great this season, which he said will be his last in the NFL. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy was asked this week if Rodgers was still the team's starter, so it wasn't completely out of the blue that he got benched.

    Recent findings suggest that it was still abrupt, and with some unusual timing. There was no time to celebrate the end of a legendary career or even realize that the snaps he took Sunday might be his last.

    It's just done, barring some other turn of events over the final few weeks of the season.

    The Steelers made the decision late Tuesday night to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers. On Wednesday morning, the team began dealing with the fallout from that decision.

    Rodgers was reportedly not in the building early Wednesday when the Steelers held their morning team meeting at 8 a.m. ET, per ESPN's Brooke Pryor.

    Additional reporting suggested Rodgers was excused from going to team facilities the day after it was announced he was benched.

    Industry observers note that at that meeting, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy officially revealed the quarterback change to the rest of the team. That decision was reportedly "not a popular" one within the locker room, per The Athletic.

    While Rodgers struggled this season, he was still well-liked by his teammates, per Pryor.

    The Pittsburgh Steelers declared Tuesday night that Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback on Friday against the Denver Broncos.

    Aaron Rodgers will be inactive.

    The Eagles listed star running back Saquon Barkley as a full practice participant on Tuesday.

    The injury report did note that it was just a walkthrough, but yesterday, when Philly did not practice, the team listed Barkley as a limited practice participant due to a neck injury as well as an illness.

    The Eagles play the Cowboys on Thursday afternoon for Thanksgiving.

    Brandon Aiyuk may have a upcoming home sooner than later.

    Industry observers note that the former 49ers receiver is scheduled to visit with the Washington Commanders. That's according to his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, who told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Aiyuk will meet with the Commanders on Wednesday.

    Ayiuk cleared waivers on Tuesday after previously being released by the 49ers, concluding a protracted and contentious breakup with the franchise.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hello, this is Priyanka Salve, writing to you from Singapore.
    • Welcome to the latest edition of "Inside India" — your one-stop destination for stories and developments from the world's fastest-growing large economy.
    • Recent findings suggest that despite 2026 being a challenging year with high global energy prices and supply chain disruptions, the Indian economy has fared surprisingly well.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hello, this is Priyanka Salve, writing to you from Singapore.

    Welcome to the latest edition of "Inside India" — your one-stop destination for stories and developments from the world's fastest-growing large economy.

    Recent findings suggest that despite 2026 being a challenging year with high global energy prices and supply chain disruptions, the Indian economy has fared surprisingly well. The auto industry, a key pillar of manufacturing and employment, has breached several records this year and is poised to report its best-ever sales.

    This week, I spoke to experts to decode what this stellar performance means for one of the world's most promising consumer markets.

    In a recent development, any thoughts on today's newsletter? Share them with the team.

    India's economy expanded at 7.8% in the June quarter, beating expectations, even as growth in several major economies cooled. Foreign portfolio investors who had been exiting Indian markets in droves for most of the year have also started returning in historic numbers.

    Recent findings suggest that and now, the world's third-largest auto market is set to for a record this year as better road connectivity, tax cuts, and easier financing options have fueled bumper sales over the last several months. That comes at a time when major auto markets across the world, from China to the U.S. have been seeing a slump in sales.

    "10 years ago, despite having the money, people did not buy cars, but now even if they don't have the money, they take financing and buy," Amar Sheth, vice president of the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations, told CNBC, pointing to the shift in consumer mindset.

    They are becoming "more optimistic" about the future and, rather than waiting, consumers are willing to take a loan and purchase something useful to them now, he adds.

    The industry body that Sheth represents noted on Monday that automakers in India were poised to sell more than 30 million vehicles in the financial year ending March 2027, dubbing the sector as a "reflection of the wider India growth story.".

    From April to October, total vehicle retail sales in India reached 18.7 million units, up 10% from a year earlier, with car, tractor and commercial vehicle sales growing more than 15%, as per FADA data.

    The optimism of the industry body is also shared by major automakers; several of whom have declared capacity expansion looks this year to meet the growing consumer demand.

    It has been revealed that japanese automakers Maruti Suzuki and Toyota blueprint to raise capacity by 1.2 million units and 200,000 units, while Korea's Hyundai Motors will add capacity for 150,000 units, as per data shared by automotive industry intelligence provider Mobility Global. Leading Indian companies Tata Motors, Mahindra & Mahindra and JSW have also revealed capacity addition plans, the data showed.

    India is the only massive auto market in the world that is growing while most others such as France, Germany, and Korea are "either declining or are flat," Puneet Gupta, director India and ASEAN at Mobility Global, told CNBC, explaining the reason behind car companies investing in the country.

    Gupta remarked that the Chinese automotive market hit an inflection point in 2007, when the GDP per capita crossed $2,500, and now India is "at a similar point." He added that government support for the auto industry would be crucial in replicating the boom seen in the Chinese auto industry.

    The catalyst for India's auto sector boom traces back to last September, when the government declared a wide range of tax cuts to spur domestic consumption.

    The auto industry contributes 7.1% to the country's gross domestic product, 49% to manufacturing GDP, 15% to goods and services tax collection, and supports 30 million jobs, as per government data.

    While the tailwinds from the tax cuts have faded, experts now believe that replacement demand and the growing reach of financing options to smaller cities will unlock the next phase of growth.

    Consumption has been strong this year as the government has partly shielded people from rising energy costs while corporates, with their strong balance sheets, have been slow to pass on price hikes, Gaura Sengupta, chief economist at India's IDFC First Bank, said.

    So far this year, wage growth has been good, the labor market has held up equity markets haven't corrected sharply, keeping the wealth effect intact, she stated, underscoring the reasons driving consumption along with easy access to credit.

    Despite the economy facing external shocks, producers are also "feeling confident to add capacity" as they have seen domestic demand sustain, Sengupta added.

    However, experts mentioned that the central bank's recent tightening of monetary policy and price hikes by automakers could slightly take the edge off the auto sales boom in the last few months of the financial year.

    While urban demand is unlikely to get affected, rural sales growth could moderate, they added.

    "Overall retail should close FY27 in high single digits," Diwakar Murugan, senior automotive analyst at Omdia, told CNBC, adding that this year's record sales are not a one-time spike but a "structural reset.".

    According to recent reports, china has changed tactics but is still thwarting India's rise, a U.S. panel saysChina is "actively working to suppress India's rise," even as the relationship between the two major Asian powers has thawed in the past year, according to a U.S. panel that sees an opening for greater outreach to India.

    It has been revealed that U.K.-India trade deal faces a stiff test over Scotch whisky import taxesWithin months of taking effect, the India-U.K. trade deal is facing an early test, as New Delhi resists extending preferential tariffs to bulk Scotch whisky imports.

    As Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    Recent findings suggest that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the fresh tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Industry observers note that implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders massive and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," remarked Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia chip sellers are seeking new buyers for the semiconductor giant's hardware, three people told CNBC, after the Trump administration tightened rules to curb Chinese companies' remote access to the most advanced artificial-intelligence systems.
    • Companies have put an unusually high volume of Nvidia graphics processing units, or GPUs, on the market since upcoming measures restricting Chinese companies renting access to advanced Nvidia chips were unveiled on Nov.
    • Jack Duhamel, president of AI infrastructure marketplace GPU Mart, and two people familiar with the matter told CNBC the surge in GPUs for sale was directly attributable to the newly introduced rule.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia chip sellers are seeking new buyers for the semiconductor giant's hardware, three people told CNBC, after the Trump administration tightened rules to curb Chinese companies' remote access to the most advanced artificial-intelligence systems.

    Companies have put an unusually high volume of Nvidia graphics processing units, or GPUs, on the market since upcoming measures restricting Chinese companies renting access to advanced Nvidia chips were unveiled on Nov. 16, the people said.

    Jack Duhamel, president of AI infrastructure marketplace GPU Mart, and two people familiar with the matter told CNBC the surge in GPUs for sale was directly attributable to the newly introduced rule. Duhamel added that one company looking to sell Nvidia chips told GPU Mart the sale was related to the new rule.

    Recent findings suggest that the two people stated it appeared chip sellers were seeking to offload them because they were originally for use in data centers in which Chinese companies would rent access. They asked not to be named because they were discussing private information.

    The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, confirmed an interim final rule as part of a clampdown on Chinese companies bypassing export controls, which effectively ban the sale of the most advanced Nvidia chips to China, by accessing them remotely in overseas data centers. The rule came into effect on Nov. 19.

    Deals to find buyers for thousands of B300 GPUs, one of Nvidia's most advanced offerings, have been floated since the rule was confirmed, said Duhamel and one of the people.

    It has been revealed that nvidia declined to comment. BIS did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

    Nvidia has been facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips.

    It has been revealed that the chip giant warned its customers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act — which has passed the House of Representatives but is yet to pass the Senate — would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services, potentially exposing both parties to "legal action," sources previously told CNBC.

    Sources indicate that in July, the U.S. accused a Chinese AI lab, Moonshot AI, of accessing Nvidia chips via a facility in Thailand. CNBC reported on Nov. 5 that the organization had sought access to the chips via data centers in Europe.

    It has been revealed that U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday that the new rule announced last week was intended to close "loopholes.".

    "For a long time, we have not allowed the sale of Blackwell chips, which are the highest AI chips or similar chips to China directly," he said.

    "Some rules were issued by the Commerce Department last week to close off indirect access, either smuggling through places like Southeast Asia or remote access from data centers in third countries.".

    In a recent development, during Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 17, then-interim CEO Colette Kress mentioned the company was still studying the controls, but expected performance to remain strong because demand for chips far exceeded supply.

    Tech Report: Robots could be doing household chores in just 1-2 years, Chinese EV firm says

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • BEIJING — The household robot could soon become a reality, Brian Gu, co-president of Xpeng, a Chinese electric car company which has entered the humanoids space, told CNBC.
    • "Maybe after successful deployment into commercial settings, maybe another one to two years, we can start thinking about deploying into home settings," Gu remarked.
    • Industry observers note that xpeng revealed its latest general-purpose humanoid robot Iron on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    BEIJING — The household robot could soon become a reality, Brian Gu, co-president of Xpeng, a Chinese electric car company which has entered the humanoids space, told CNBC.

    "Maybe after successful deployment into commercial settings, maybe another one to two years, we can start thinking about deploying into home settings," Gu remarked. "Technology is moving at a much faster clip.".

    Industry observers note that xpeng revealed its latest general-purpose humanoid robot Iron on Wednesday. The company plans to start training the robot as a store assistant in its retail car locations in the first quarter next year, after starting mass production in January. Sales are set to begin in the second quarter, with deliveries expected later in the year.

    Founded in 2014 as an electric car organization, Xpeng beat Tesla to rolling out driver-assist in mainland China. The Chinese automaker has launched its own artificial intelligence chips. It's also expanded into personal flying vehicles and robotics. The robotics unit this summer raised $900 million at a $6.3 billion valuation in its first funding round, led by IDG Capital.

    Investors, however, appear to be a tad skeptical about the developments at Xpeng, with the downturn in the Chinese auto market also weighing on the company. Xpeng's shares, listed in both New York and Hong Kong, have dropped more than 55% this year amid broad sector declines.

    According to recent reports, china's humanoid industry has faced more regulatory scrutiny on financing in recent months after Unitree's high-profile IPO and stock slump, as well as a rush of capital into the sector. That's all raised questions about commercialization and the efficacy of the core tech.

    In a recent development, gu said Xpeng's robotics stands out for its rare combination of the hardware, software and real-life use cases. He's expecting to add more investors after Iron's planned commercial launch next year.

    According to recent reports, "You can always make the head talk, you can always make the leg run, you can always make the hands to do certain tasks," Gu mentioned. "But doing a task while you're walking and answering questions at the same time, that's the most challenging part. And then doing everything well, not falling down, not getting distracted. The model has to work in sync.".

    According to recent reports, most humanoid robot startups, especially in China, focus on a portion of the tech, such as hands or the artificial intelligence-powered brain. Some in the industry also see themselves as original equipment manufacturers, with another company tying the parts together for the finished robot.

    But that may be easier noted than done.

    Xpeng's co-founder and CEO He Xiaopeng, a software engineer, always thought that software could solve "everything,'" Gu noted. "And after he got into the EV business he realized how hard it is to make hardware ... really do the things that you want to do safely and consistently.".

    On Wednesday, Xpeng declared its "Turing Physical AI Architecture" for using AI and real-time decision-making tech to control cars and humanoids.

    Gu told CNBC that Xpeng's robotics development only needs the driver-assist chips, which the company already has, indicating limited impact from U.S. restrictions on advanced Nvidia chip sales to China.

    "Right now we don't see any change to our supply chain, and also ability to have these chips.".

    In 2023, Xpeng's then-head of autonomous driving, Xinzhou Wu, left to lead Nvidia's automotive chip business.

    Industry observers note that as Xpeng ramps up its humanoid robotics business, Gu said the company's existing work in autonomous driving technology translates easily to a newly introduced product line — with far higher profit margins. "It's much easier to be profitable for the robotics business than the autos business.".

    Robotics will likely become a meaningful part of Xpeng's business in two to three years, Gu remarked, with profitability coming as soon as next year. That value will "dramatically" increase with robots entering households, he said.

    It has been revealed that but Gu noted that compared to commercial environments, homes require robots to act safely around elderly people, children and pets, in addition to reacting to emergency situations. That increases requirements for battery power and performance consistency, he said.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte issued a joint statement on Thursday urging Russia not to take any actions, intentionally or otherwise, that would further expand the Ukraine war.
    • The statement comes as Ukraine's allies sound the alarm over Russia's growing threat to European security and just one week after Trump's historic trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Asia.
    • Trump and Rutte described their meeting at the Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida on Wednesday as "very impactful," with Russia's nearly five-year-long war in Ukraine and the Iran war among the key topics of conversation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    U.S. President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte issued a joint statement on Thursday urging Russia not to take any actions, intentionally or otherwise, that would further expand the Ukraine war.

    The statement comes as Ukraine's allies sound the alarm over Russia's growing threat to European security and just one week after Trump's historic trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Asia.

    Trump and Rutte described their meeting at the Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida on Wednesday as "very impactful," with Russia's nearly five-year-long war in Ukraine and the Iran war among the key topics of conversation.

    "We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible," Trump and Rutte mentioned in their statement.

    Moreover, the two discussed the importance of further increasing defense spending as well as investment in the defense industrial base in both the U.S. and NATO countries, according to the statement.

    Trump also said in a post on Truth Social Thursday that he "briefed NATO on the tremendous progress" being made in growing defense production, noting that the focus will be on building Patriot air defense systems, THAAD systems and Tomahawk cruise missiles, as well as "many new Weapons, both Offensive and Defensive, that have not yet been viewed by the Public, or other Countries.".

    It has been revealed that "There has never been a time when the United States has produced more Military Equipment or Munitions than now. Our 'cupboard' will soon be full and, when it is, our Allies and Partners throughout the World will be benefitting greatly," he said in the post.

    Trump's meeting with Xi and Putin, in which he described the Russian president as his "friend," sparked alarm among European lawmakers about Washington's commitment to transatlantic security.

    NATO's Rutte, a seasoned diplomat known as a consensus builder during his nearly 14 years as Dutch prime minister, has repeatedly sought to de-escalate tensions in the alliance and frequently used flattery to win over the U.S. president.

    While some have questioned whether this approach has delivered any tangible benefits, Trump has previously described Rutte as a "great leader" and NATO's "biggest asset.".

    Russia has stepped up its attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure in recent weeks, with further attacks on the central Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih overnight disrupting power supplies and bringing municipal electric public transport to a standstill, according to Oleksandr Vilkul, head of Kryvyi ​Rih's defense council.

    Ukrainian officials on Wednesday stated Russian attacks on the country's power sector had damaged energy infrastructure and caused power outages in five regions as cold winter weather sets in.

    In a recent development, german Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Wednesday accused the Kremlin of "escalating" threats toward European security, citing actions in the Baltic region, Poland and on the Black Sea, and adding that "Russia knows exactly what it wants.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.
    • On platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026.
    • Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    On platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    "The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note mentioned.

    According to recent reports, the Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

    In that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

    📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6454 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.
    • Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.
    • Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

    Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

    Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

    Recent findings suggest that really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

    They were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

    Recent findings suggest that dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt.

    “I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle mentioned quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”.

    Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

    No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

    Industry observers note that one of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

    How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address swiftly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

    It has been revealed that off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

    In a recent development, an electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F.

    As Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

    In a recent development, “We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”.

    What could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

    This, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

    According to recent reports, cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v.

    But parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

    It has been revealed that "Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK.

    “We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola said. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

    “You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”.

    Why they didn’t follow the proposal that had been set is something that Iraola must address, but he will be relieved that the days spent this week are not dissecting a defeat, as Wissa should have wrapped up the contest, only for Alisson to make a brilliant save to thwart the Congolese striker.

    Industry observers note that those missed chances should not have mattered but in the final throes, Hall misjudged the angle Muñoz attacked him from, he got his challenge wrong and, after a pause, Attwell pointed to the spot. Given the agony Liverpool have inflicted, the outcome was as clear as black and white.

    “We scored at the end, so you have a better taste,” Iraola said. “Before the game, we wouldn’t have signed for this result. It’s a reward. It’s only a point, but at least it’s something that’s deserved.”.

    Plenty would contest his conclusion. Liverpool got away with it – and Iraola is about to find the hard work is only just beginning.

    A really soft one, if you give that, they’ll be more in the future, I’m not a fan of that.

    Their heads are a little down but we know we had many challenges, we’re in a huge transition phase at the moment.

    It’s a brave project but I like the challenge, working with young lads, they were tired. Lewis Miley just came back from an injury but they did an amazing job and it’s just about getting adapted to the league.

    The crowd here is unbelievable and the quality. Every change can be decisive and it’s something I really enjoy. We’re clear in our approach and you can adjust in the game if you strategy ahead.

    It’s not the result you want, but scoring in the last minute gives us a better feeling. I value that the players never gave up. I’m sure we had more chances, it’s unfair they’re winning very early and overall, I think we’ve had the better chances.

    We were probably in the first half not finishing anything, we had a lot of balls on the edge but we needed to shoot. We don’t finish play and then they win on the counter-attack.

    The players coming from the bench gave us energy and you can feel the way we want to play.

    Overall, we played a lot in their half and had good moments and phases on the ball. The first goal was more difficult to defend, Anthony Elanga is a fast player. The second, I think we had the numbers but sometimes you have to finish the play and try and win the ball.

    According to recent reports, what a special club, what a special man, that’s why we gave him a substantial credit. The fans were unbelievable today. I think we gave them so much back today and that’s what we need to give them all season.

    Sources indicate that we know we needed to give the fans something after this period so that’s why we tried to start fast. The fans pushed us until the end.

    It was my best [performance for Newcastle] so far. Upcoming manager, new role. I’m so pleased to be here. I hope today I demonstrated I’m really happy.

    In a recent development, it’s rough, especially 30 seconds before the end of the game, but that’s a huge step for us. That’s the mentality we need to have through the season. The manager came three weeks ago and gave us a lot of information. Now we show on the pitch we are ready for the season. We needed this win to make a statement but in the end we draw. We have so much to work on.

    To be honest, I didn’t even hear the referee’s whistle. I had to look at him if I can go. I was practising a lot during the pre-season. We didn’t have any penalties during games, but in training. We need to take the positivity of the first game and move on.

    In a recent development, more than 50,000 fans in the stadium against you. You can’t hear your own voice. That’s why I love football and that’s why I am doing it.

    To come here is always tough. Everybody knows the [Newcastle] fans are unbelievable. They have a great team and a manager - fresh but he has proven himself in many other clubs. But we were prepared and we needed to be closer to each other under a new manager as well. We needed to know what was going on in the game. It’s a good thing coming back into the game after 2-1 down.

    Sources indicate that if I am honest, we should have won. But that’s football. You don’t win easy in the Premier League - doesn’t matter who you play against. We have to be aware of that and we need to take care in the next game.
