    Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

    📅 26 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest significant-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his upcoming club.
    • Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.
    • But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest significant-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his upcoming club.

    Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

    But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

    According to recent reports, “A perfect day for him,” remarked De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

    According to recent reports, “We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”.

    "What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX.

    Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

    The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

    A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

    In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

    Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

    Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

    According to recent reports, what a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs.

    Sources indicate that “We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”.

    It has been revealed that cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

    Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

    In a recent development, buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”.

    Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

    Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW.

    According to recent reports, the victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

    “Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against massive teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”.

    It has been revealed that “He did great when he came on. He is going to be a joy for all of us to watch. I am sure he will be a fan favourite. He demonstrated what a player he is tonight. To get one goal and an assist on his debut is great.”.

    Premier League: Brighton, Arsenal, Brentford, Everton, Hull, Ipswich, Manchester City, Liverpool, Newcastle, Bournemouth, Sunderland, Crystal Palace, Manchester United, Coventry, Tottenham, Aston Villa.

    Championship: Millwall, Wolves, Middlesbrough, Sheffield United, West Ham, Lincoln, Norwich.

    League One: Bradford, Leyton Orient, Peterborough, Reading, Barnsley.

    Still to play: Chelsea v Luton, Fulham v AFC Wimbledon.

    The teams in the hat for the League Cup third round will found out who they will face very shortly and we will let you know all the ties for the third round.

    Bradford 0 Burnley 0 (Bradford won 4-2 on penalties)Newcastle 3 West Brom 2Tottenham 5 Charlton 1Preston 0 Everton 4.

    Possession: Tottenham 73%-27% CharltonShots: 20-6Shots on target: 11-4Corners: 11-6Touches in opposition box: 45-8.

    It is all over in north London and Tottenham have booked their place in the third round of the League Cup with a comfortable 5-1 win over Charlton.

    Three added minutes in north London.

    Newcastle have just about got past West Brom, winning 3-2 in the end, and they book their place in the third round.

    At least the travelling Charlton fans have something to cheer about even if their side are being dumped out of the League Cup. A corner from the left comes to the back post, where Jones rises highest to head it between Kinsky’s legs and into the Tottenham net.

    It has been revealed that savio thinks he has his second in quick succession but it will go down as Davies’ goal. Savio’s shot was on target but it deflects off Davies and goes in for Tottenham’s fifth on the night.

    The Brazilian signed just yesterday but he now has a first Tottenham goal to his name. He cuts inside from the right and drives across the face of the penalty area before firing at the near post, beating Brooks. Tottenham are cruising into the third round and their newest signing scores on his debut.

    "What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX.

    Tottenham are cruising into the third round and so are Everton, who lead Preston by the same scoreline. Newcastle lead West Brom 3-2 whilst it is still 0-0 between Bradford and Burnley.

    Change for Tottenham as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel.

    Tel crosses from the left side of the box and picks out Savio, who attempts an audacious flick that does not come off.

    West Brom were not back on level terms for long as Barnes has his second of the game and Newcastle lead 3-2 with under 10 minutes remaining.

    Charlton have barely threatened the Tottenham goal tonight but that is a decent opportunity for Leaburn, who is played in down the right and forces Kinsky into a decent save.

    Savio is straight into the action with good work down the right and squares it for Tel, whose shot is straight at Brooks.

    Savio is on for his Tottenham debut and replaces Solanke. Savio only joined Tottenham yesterday but makes his first appearance for the club tonight.

    Recent findings suggest that newcastle had fought from 1-0 down against West Brom to lead 2-1 but Hall has just given away a penalty for the second time in a matter of days having also conceded one in the dying moments of their 2-2 draw against Liverpool on Sunday. Price has stepped up to score his second of the game to bring West Brom level at 2-2 with just over 10 minutes to go.

    Recent findings suggest that the Austrian defender has just come on and, with his first touch, puts Tottenham 3-0 up. Fernandes’ free-kick from just outside the box on the right is met by Danso, who attacks it and his header finds the bottom corner. You have to say that goal was coming. Danso has hurt himself as there was a clash of heads as he met the delivery and receives treatment to his head.

    Recent findings suggest that kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW.

    Roberto De Zerbi is turning to his bench and making a triple change as Van de Ven, Danso and Porro come on.

    Charlton are also making a triple change of their own.

    Sources indicate that gray is found on the left side of the Charlton penalty area and he drives his shot towards goal, forcing Brooks into a decent save. Tottenham are pushing for that third goal.

    A cross is sent in from the right and it comes to Tel, who volleys first time but it is a fairly routine save for Brooks in the Charlton goal.

    Tottenham are starting to ramp up the pressure as they go in search of a third goal. As it stands, the only side that looks like scoring is Tottenham.

    Plenty of cheers from the home fans as Savio is out to warm up. Will Roberto De Zerbi turn to the Brazilian and give him his debut tonight?

    One of the new laws brought in this season is to speed up throw-ins and Gray falls foul of taking too long, with Charlton then being given the throw-in.

    Tel decides to shoot from range after Charlton clear a corner but the Frenchman’s effort is straight at Brooks.

    Play has resumed in north London, with Tottenham 2-0 up over Charlton.

    According to recent reports, they are back under way at St James’ Park and there has been a goal within a few minutes of the second half starting. Newcastle were 1-0 down against West Brom but they now lead 2-1 thanks to Barnes’ goal.

    Possession: Tottenham 76%-24% CharltonShots: 9-2Shots on target: 4-1Corners: 7-2Touches in opposition box: 25-2.

    Industry observers note that the first half in north London is brought to an end and Tottenham take a 2-0 lead into the break thanks to goals from Moore and Solanke. Tottenham looked rather lethargic for a lot of that first half but two goals in quick succession has Roberto De Zerbi’s side in control. As the players head off, the DJ pays homage to the late Dolly Parton by blasting out Nine to Five.

    Whilst they are still in added time in north London, it is half-time at St James’ Park and Newcastle are level 1-1 with West Brom.

    Apter is booked for cynically tripping up Udogie.

    Due to a few Charlton injuries, there will be six added minutes.

    Industry observers note that like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Tottenham have their second just before the break. Charlton fail to clear their lines inside their own box before Solanke volleys in on the swivel from the penalty spot. Charlton will feel that was definitely an avoidable goal.

    Tottenham had looked rather lethargic but they take the lead in emphatic style. The 19-year-old cuts inside from the right and comes across the face of the Charlton penalty area. Moore then strikes it powerfully with his left foot and the ball flies into the roof of the net. Could Brooks have done better in the Charlton goal? Moore will not care.

    Sources indicate that what a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs.

    Tottenham are presently too slow in possession and are not moving the ball promptly enough, meaning it is easier for Charlton to defend.

    West Brom had taken the lead at St James’ Park but Newcastle are back on level terms through summer signing Toure.

    A corner from the right ends up coming out to the edge of the box, where Tel takes it first time but his volley goes a long way wide. That moment sums up Tottenham’s evening thus far.

    Solanke has a shot from the edge of the box blocked before Gray’s effort with the outside of his right foot is saved well by Brooks down to his left. That looked like it was creeping in so Brooks had to get a hand to that.

    Charlton play the corner short and eventually the ball comes in. Asiimwe meets it and has a good chance from eight yards out but his header goes just wide. That was a decent chance for Charlton.

    In a recent development, the first booking of the night goes the way of the hosts as Bergvall cynically takes down Apter as the Charlton man drove towards the Tottenham penalty area. You feel like Charlton need to take advantage of opportunities like this if they want to win this tie. The ball is clipped in and it comes off Van Hecke’s head for a corner. Tottenham clear their lines initially but Charlton keep it alive. Docherty strikes it first time from the edge of the Tottenham box and forces Kinsky into a good save diving to his left.

    It has been revealed that that probably sums up Tottenham’s night thus far. Davies pings a lovely diagonal ball out to Moore in space down Tottenham’s right. Moore waits for the overlapping run of Gray before playing the pass but Gray’s attempted cross from the right side of the box is terrible and goes behind for a goal kick. Roberto De Zerbi is promptly out of his seat!

    Recent findings suggest that roberto De Zerbi was keen to see his side show a reaction to their defeat at Brentford on Saturday. Unsurprisingly, they are dominating possession but have not posed much of a threat going forward.

    There has been a goal at St James’ Park and it is the visitors West Brom who have taken the lead over Newcastle. Price has scored directly from a free-kick and the Championship side lead.

    It has been revealed that A sensational free-kick from Isaac Price to give West Brom the lead at St. James' Park! 🤯Watch the Carabao Cup here! - https://t.co/4BMyhp9stB pic.twitter.com/Pnt78LWFN6.

    It has been revealed that things have just gone from bad to worse for Charlton. Whilst one of their centre-backs is being stretchered off in Sichenje, their other centre-half Koumetio, who used to be on the books at Liverpool, is also down. Koumetio, like Sichenje, is going to come off. McNamara and Jones, who like Koumetio used to be at Liverpool, are coming on. Charlton have had to change both centre-backs inside the opening quarter of an hour.

    It has been revealed that sichenje did try to continue but he has gone back down again and his night appears to be over. The question will be has he done more damage to his knee trying to play on? The stretcher is being brought on and it will be a sorry end to his night.

    In a recent development, moore wins Tottenham a corner out on the right, which summer signing Fernandes will take. His delivery is headed away and the danger is gone.

    Recent findings suggest that sichenje has now got back to his feet so he may have avoided a serious injury but we will see if he can continue. It looks like he will try to continue at least.

    In a recent development, play is halted as Charlton defender Sichenje looks to be in a lot of pain as he bangs the ground in frustration. It appears to be his left knee and the visitors may be forced into an early change.

    Inside the opening minute, Solanke thinks he will have a chance on goal as the ball is played in behind but there is too much on it and the ball goes through to Brooks in the Charlton goal.

    We are under way in north London.

    Industry observers note that both sides emerge from the tunnel at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and we are just moments away from kick-off north London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

We need to be organised and in the moments we have we want to use our structure to carry a threat. We want to see our structure coming through because we want to evolve. We are a way off these yet, but that is eventually the goal.”.

    Industry observers note that after nine years at Anfield, Andy Robertson has swapped Liverpool for Tottenham this summer. He started for Tottenham against Brentford and is on the bench tonight ahead of what could be his first home game for the club.

    Omar Marmoush will undergo a medical at Tottenham Hotspur on Wednesday on loan with an obligation to pay Manchester City £60m for the Egypt forward next summer.

    Marmoush will become the second signing from City this week after Savinho – who has asked to be referred to as Sávio – completed his move.

    City signed Marmoush two seasons ago from Eintracht Frankfurt for £59m and the German club do not have a sell-on clause, meaning they will not receive a fee from the deal.

    According to recent reports, our Spurs side to face Charlton! 📋🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/yQuEVgkHbm.

    It has been revealed that A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

    Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

    Recent findings suggest that “I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a significant player for us.

    Sources indicate that “I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”.

    Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

    It has been revealed that charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

    “We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most vital.”.

    #143271. Breaking: Nvidia's billion-dollar board bet: Who's protected as lawsuits mount?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (962 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Nvidia's billion-dollar board bet: Who's protected as lawsuits mount?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (962 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia, after President Donald Trump urged the tech giant's board to rehire Huang.
    • Industry observers note that "Clearly they caved to external pressure," said Betsy Atkins, an author and longtime public-manufacturer director.
    • Industry observers note that california Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia misrepresented information to investors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia, after President Donald Trump urged the tech giant's board to rehire Huang. But investigations into the company, its executive leadership and its board continue as outside criticism mounts.

    Industry observers note that "Clearly they caved to external pressure," said Betsy Atkins, an author and longtime public-manufacturer director. "The board failed," she said, when it initially allowed Huang's removal. "The board's role is to think of all stakeholders.".

    Industry observers note that california Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia misrepresented information to investors. "There is classic corporate securities law on the books in California that prevents investors and the public from being misled by companies," Bonta stated on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Tuesday.

    Directors are already defendants in a shareholder lawsuit accusing them of failing to oversee Nvidia. A separate securities class action targets the company and Huang, its co-founder.

    Now the board’s insurance choices are part of the story. A risk advisor with direct knowledge of Nvidia’s coverage indicates the tech giant built an approximately $1 billion D&O tower, insurance jargon for directors and officers insurance policies from different companies that combine to cover one massive risk.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia "loves insurance," the advisor said. “They buy insurance as if they have no balance sheet.” A billion-dollar tower would essentially mean Nvidia "bought the market," purchasing all the coverage it could get, according to an industry expert with 25 years working in financial insurance. The expert asked not to be named out of concern for past or potential future clients.

    Sources indicate that but Nvidia directed all that coverage to Side A only, according to CNBC's source. Side A protects directors and officers personally when the organization cannot indemnify them. Side B covers the company for legal defense costs or settlements on behalf of directors and officers, and Side C protects the company when it's named as a defendant in a suit such as a securities claim.

    The risk advisor says Nvidia believed it had "the war chest" to protect itself against a securities class action suit.

    That choice is raising questions about whether the board protected itself at the company’s expense. CNBC asked Nvidia for comment but received no response.

    An insurance CEO characterized a billion-dollar policy as a lot of coverage, but said a Side A-only allocation was a surprising move because it results in imbalanced coverage, protecting only directors.

    It has been revealed that that structure is not automatically a governance failure, according to a D&O insurance expert with long experience in coverage for banks, drugmakers and other businesses that often face litigation. Side A-only programs are common among companies with the capital to manage the corporate risk internally.

    "For a firm with Nvidia’s resources, retaining the company-side risk can make financial sense," the advisor mentioned. It's Side A D&O that's "imperative to corporate governance.".

    Sources indicate that "It is a capital-allocation decision," the expert told me. The organization decides that buying insurance for its own balance sheet is not worth the premium. In other words, Side B and Side C are considered too expensive for the coverage the company gets.

    The question for shareholders is whether the board’s decision to hold that risk was a sound use of the tech giant’s resources and whether the company can absorb the costs if the claims grow.

    A shareholder derivative complaint filed Nov. 11 names Huang, directors and other officers. It alleges that they failed to oversee risks involving Huang’s relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang and made misleading statements. It also alleges that some defendants sold roughly $2 billion in Nvidia stock while holding material nonpublic information. Those remain allegations, not findings.

    It has been revealed that A separate securities class action, filed Nov. 9, names Nvidia and Huang. It seeks damages for investors who bought Nvidia shares between Oct. 9, 2025, and Nov. 8, 2026, alleging the company and Huang misled investors.

    The distinction matters: The derivative suit is brought on Nvidia’s behalf, while the class action seeks recovery for investors.

    According to recent reports, "Insurance is already at work," claims Michel Léonard, chief economist at the Insurance Information Institute, describing standard policy mechanics, not Nvidia’s specific policy. "Once the suit is filed, D&O starts paying defense costs, long before anyone proves anything.".

    Recent findings suggest that A claim still has to meet the policy’s terms, and defense costs can reduce the remaining limits. Nor does a drop in Nvidia’s market value by itself establish an insurable loss. Plaintiffs would need to prove legally recoverable damages; the policy would respond only to covered losses.

    The board has already taken steps it claims are aimed at accountability. Nvidia declared an independent investigation on Nov. 8, and independent directors retained outside counsel two days later. Huang resigned as CEO and a director on Nov. 11; the board appointed CFO Colette Kress interim CEO. Nvidia noted it had no reason to believe national security or tech giant secrets had been compromised by Huang's extramarital relationships.

    Atkins, who joined the board of Wynn Resorts in 2018 after founder Steve Wynn resigned, argues that allegations are not conclusions and that boards should also weigh governance concerns against the value a founder brings to a firm’s innovation. Nvidia's investigation is continuing even as Huang resumes leadership.

    “Will companies’ hyper-accelerated innovation speed be the same without them? I don’t think so,” remarked Atkins, author of "Don't Waste a Board Seat: A Decision-Maker's Guide to Choosing Directors Who Create Value.".

    Nvidia’s 2026 proxy also indicates the organization has indemnity agreements with its directors and officers — separate from its insurance. Those agreements provide for the company to cover certain costs and liabilities when the law permits.

    #143260. Semiconductor chips are the new oil. Here's why

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (513 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Semiconductor chips are the new oil. Here's why

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (513 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The artificial intelligence boom has pushed semiconductors past oil and gas in global export value for the first time, according to a Deutsche Bank analysis of International Trade Centre data.
    • Yet the milestone arrives at an awkward moment, just as investors reassess the outlook for artificial intelligence spending and drive down the price of semiconductor stocks.
    • Nvidia soared more than 31% Monday after the leading maker of artificial intelligence chips had fallen for a seventh straight week, plunging 46% during that stretch.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The artificial intelligence boom has pushed semiconductors past oil and gas in global export value for the first time, according to a Deutsche Bank analysis of International Trade Centre data.

    Yet the milestone arrives at an awkward moment, just as investors reassess the outlook for artificial intelligence spending and drive down the price of semiconductor stocks. Last week, before Monday's breathtaking reversal, semiconductor stocks suffered their worst weekly loss in a quarter century, with the PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOX) plunging nearly 11% last Friday alone, capping a more than 17% weekly decline.

    Nvidia soared more than 31% Monday after the leading maker of artificial intelligence chips had fallen for a seventh straight week, plunging 46% during that stretch. Then it fell again, dropping almost 10% on Tuesday and Wednesday. Advanced Micro Devices tumbled 20% in two days last Thursday and Friday. Micron Technology sank 27% over the seven days ended last Friday.

    Recent findings suggest that "For decades we've talked about the petrodollar. Perhaps increasingly we need to think about the chip dollar," Jim Reid, global head of macro and thematic research at Deutsche Bank wrote in a report this month.

    Semiconductor exports overtook oil and gas for the first time during the January-March quarter of 2026, reaching about $1.61 trillion, compared with $1.53 trillion for oil and gas, the report remarked, using four-quarter rolling totals.

    The gap widened in the second quarter, when semiconductor exports totaled about $1.60 trillion and oil and gas exports reached about $1.47 trillion. Disruptions to oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz after the Iran war helped widen the gap. Daily oil flows through the Strait collapsed nearly 77%, to 4.9 million barrels in the second quarter of 2026 from 21.6 million barrels in the fourth quarter of 2025, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

    Yet the demand for semiconductors has proven insatiable in the face of soaring data center construction, boosting global trade in the increasingly scarce AI component. Hundreds of billions of dollars of orders for graphics processing units and data centers aim at providing AI computing power, Rothschild & Co. Redburn wrote in a report last Thursday.

    "Compute will be the fresh commodity fueling this transformation on a global scale," Rothschild analyst Cara Thomson said.

    The shift toward chips has macroeconomic implications just as the explosion in oil trade did in the 1970s.

    Recent findings suggest that oil-exporting countries historically recycled much of their surpluses into the purchase of U.S. Treasuries and other bonds, helping finance U.S. deficits and underpin demand for other government debt.

    Industry observers note that reid at Deutsche Bank mentioned that since semiconductor-surplus countries in Asia are more closely tied to U.S. tech companies, some chip-export earnings could flow back into U.S. technology stocks, startups and data centers, further helping to finance the AI investment cycle.

    The changing dynamics in global trade could also tilt the mix of global financial flows, Reid said. "So welcome to the chip-dollar era: potentially more growth, more excitement, more volatility, and structurally higher yields" in corporate and government debt.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

    Recent findings suggest that that made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

    According to recent reports, not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

    It has been revealed that loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an problem is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    The Philadelphia 76ers could be short-staffed when they take on the Indiana Pacers in NBA Cup play on Friday night.

    It has been revealed that shooting guard Jaylen Brown has already been ruled out with a hamstring injury. Center Joel Embiid is listed as questionable due to a lingering illness that has sidelined him for Philadelphia's last two games.

    Sources indicate that brown picked up the hamstring glitch in Wednesday's NBA Cup win over the Miami Heat. He left the game late in the first half and did not return. The guard missed two games last week with a left hamstring strain, but returned to action against the Portland Trail Blazers and played 29 minutes.

    Toward the end of the first half, the Philadelphia guard reached toward his left hamstring and shook his head before checking himself out of the game.

    Embiid is dealing with an illness, though not much has been released about what symptoms he may be dealing with. Regardless, he has missed two consecutive games. The center was listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Heat, but was downgraded before the game.

    It has been revealed that with no Embiid and no Brown for a half, LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey took over and led the 76ers to a win over the Heat on Wednesday. James logged his first triple-double as a 76er with 25 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists. Maxey added 30 points, 4 rebounds and 6 assists.

    In a recent development, the win moved Philadelphia to 15-4. Friday's game against Indiana is the front end of a back-to-back, and a win would help the 76ers clinch their NBA Cup group.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.
    • Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.
    • Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

    Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

    Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

    Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

    Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

    During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

    Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

    Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

    Recent findings suggest that verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

    It has been revealed that verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

    Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a major statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

    It has been revealed that verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

    Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

    In a recent development, that brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

    The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

    For the middle course of today's Thanksgiving slate, the NFL is serving up a rivalry, with the Dallas Cowboys hosting the Philadelphia Eagles.

    The NFL's fiercest rivalry has a little less pizzazz this season: The Eagles are 3-7, the Cowboys are 5-6 and both have glaring weaknesses (Dallas' defense, Philadelphia's quarterback situation) that have hampered their play heading into the final stretch.

    Recent findings suggest that the Eagles' latest solution under center, Joe Milton III, follows up his surprising win against the Steelers with a return to Dallas, after starting the 2026 season on the Cowboys' practice squad. Though the Dallas offense is likely to keep up their strong pace, the issues in the Cowboys' defense might be enough to give Milton a revenge game to remember.

    Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Eagles and Cowboys face off on Thanksgiving, airing on Fox.

    Joe Milton is playing motivated football against his former team.

    Milton fired another laser to the end zone and this one went to a leaping Makai Lemon, the Eagles' first-round rookie.

    It has been revealed that philadelphia went for two, and converted but there was a flag on the play for offensive holding. The Eagles opted to still go for it, but the pass was knocked away.

    Dallas will get the ball with just over 2 minutes left, clinging to a 2-point lead.

    Brandon Aubrey, one of the best kickers in the league, missed a 40-yard field goal.

    The ball wasn't tipped, but it took off toward the uprights and then screamed left. The replay demonstrated the laces of the ball were facing in toward the kicker, which could have played a factor.

    Eagles take over with 3:23 left, trailing by 8.

    Recent findings suggest that the Eagles were facing third and 15. Milton tried to find a receiver down the field, but he threw into triple coverage and it was picked off.

    It was a wild play for Dallas who had a late sub and the player had barely come on the field and blitzed from the sideline, causing pressure on Milton.

    Dallas takes over with just over 7 minutes left in the game, leading by 8.

    Smith only missed one play and is back in the game after an extended delay while a Cowboys defender was tended to by trainers for an injury of their own.

    Eagles quarterback Joe Milton was again trying to throw a deep pass to DeVonta Smith.

    The wideout was in double coverage, and he went into the air to try to catch it, but got turned and landed hard on his back.

    He remained down and was reaching at his back. Trainers helped him to his feet and off the field. Smith left the field, jogged a little on the sideline and then went into the medical tent.

    Eagles punt returner Britain Covey took a hard hit on the punt return and it looked like the ball may have become dislodged.

    It looked like it could have been a fumble in real time, but replays showed that Covey either was down before losing it, or had regained possession.

    Regardless, Dallas threw the challenge flag, for real this time.

    The call was upheld on the field.

    In a recent development, the Cowboys ran a trick play on third and 18. Dak Prescott hit George Pickens for a quick pass.

    Pickens then all of a sudden passed it across the field to Hunter Luepke who weaved through defenders and ran the field all the way for a touchdown, even jumping into the Salvation Army red kettle.

    Industry observers note that there was a flag on the play. Pickens' pass was ruled to be a forward pass. Not only did the touchdown not count, but it resulted in a loss of down so the Steelers had to punt.

    "Anything you can do, I can do better" - Joe Milton probably.

    All of a sudden this game got interesting.

    In a recent development, after Dak Prescott's rushing touchdown, the Eagles took over. Philadelphia needed just three plays after a big kick return to score.

    Quarterback Joe Milton hit DeVonta Smith for a four-yard gain, and then on the next play the duo picked up 23 yards.

    Milton and the offense was on the 15-yard line and the quarterback took it himself and ran the ball in.

    It has been revealed that the Eagles opted to go for two, but the conversion failed. Dallas leads 38-30 with 9:09 left in the game.

    The Cowboys once had a 21-point lead and watched it nearly disappear as Dallas' most recent drive started with just a 7-point lead.

    Sources indicate that dak Prescott leaned on CeeDee Lamb to get the Cowboys down the field as the star wide receiver came down with a huge 39-yard reception to flip the field. Lamb then added a 12-yard gain later in the drive.

    The Cowboys found the end zone as Prescott took off down the sideline. He dove for the end zone and managed to get the ball to cross the goal line in bounds while absorbing a hit for the 14-yard score.

    Dallas leads 38-24 with 10:11 left in regulation.

    Dallas was facing third-and-one, and the handoff went to Javonte Williams. He was stuffed at the line and couldn't convert.

    The Cowboys offense lined up to try to get the Eagles to jump but they didn't. Dallas took the delay of game and lined up to punt.

    In a recent development, the Philadelphia special teams unit got home and blocked the punt. It bounced in the Eagles' favor and Philly was able to recover it and walk it in for the touchdown.

    After the extra-point game it is all of a sudden a 7-point game.

    Joe Milton and DeVonta Smith have been must-watch in this game.

    Milton rolled to the right on this play and threw a rocket while on the run. He hit an open DeVonta Smith who was able to come back, catch the ball and get into the end zone.

    With the extra point, Philly now trails 31-17.

    Cowboys rookie wide receiver Camden Brown had his first career reception to start the drive, and it was a big one for 19 yards.

    That was the highlight of the possession, though, as Dallas got into Brandon Aubrey's field goal range. The star kicker was good from 59 yards out, and Dallas now leads 31-10 with 3:30 left in the third quarter.

    After the Cowboys' latest punt, the Eagles had a chance to try and spark some momentum. Will Shipley picked up 10 yards on two carries, but that is where the drive ended.

    Milton was sacked for a loss of 10, Shipley picked up three yards on a carry and then Joe Milton had a deep incompletion bringing up the punt.

    Sources indicate that dallas had scored touchdowns on back-to-back drives to end the first half. That momentum was not sustained starting the second half.

    The Cowboys had a major splash play with Dak Prescott hitting CeeDee Lamb for 22 yards. After that though, it was a loss of five on a run, a gain of eight on the next play and then a sack to force a punt.

    According to recent reports, joe Milton began the second half by finding DeVonta Smith for a five-yard gain. On second down, he was sacked for a nine-yard loss, then missed Elijah Moore on third down.

    Milton's touchdown pass at the end of the first half set a team record.

    According to Next Gen Stats, his pass traveled 64.4 yards in air distance, making it the longest pass TD for an Eagles QB in the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016).

    We head to halftime with the first half being all Cowboys.

    Dallas leads 28-10, and the Eagles will get the ball coming out of the half, following an extended halftime show featuring country music singer Miranda Lambert.

    Javonte Williams can not be stopped.

    After CeeDee Lamb was whistled for Offensive Pass Interference on the previous play, the Cowboys faced third and goal from the 12-yard line.

    Dak Prescott checked down to Javonte Williams who cut and dove for the end zone, crossing the plane for the score.

    After the extra point, Dallas leads 28-10 with 4 seconds to go in the first half.

    The Cowboys have gotten to the goal line yet again, but largely because of the Eagles secondary.

    On second and eight earlier in the drive, Riq Woolen was called for defensive pass interference on George Pickens, giving Dallas 10 yards.

    On the very next play, CeeDee Lamb got a DPI call from Quinyon Mitchell that gave Dallas 29 yards and the ball at the goal line.

    39 yards in two plays, both incomplete passes for the offense, but they were the best plays of the drive.

Further, the asking price on Arizona's end is "very high," reports FanSided. Still, plenty of teams are said to be interested.

    According to recent reports, marte, 33, has five years and $91.75 million left on his deal. He finished third in MVP voting in 2024, was a highly productive All-Star in 2025, but some challenges arose in 2026, including several no-indicates. He hit .249/.316/.432 (107 OPS+) with 2.5 WAR and some possible clubhouse baggage.

    The Mets are planning a Zoom meeting with Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the New York Post. This won't have an impact on their pursuit of Tarik Skubal, just in case anyone is curious.

    Taira, 27, has been one of the top pitchers in Japan's NPB for years. Last season, in 23 starts, he had a 1.36 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 141 strikeouts in 146 innings. He's had a sub-2.00 ERA four of the last five seasons, with the exception being a 2.40 in 2023.

    According to recent reports, CBS Sports ranked Taira as the No. 19 free agent available this winter:.

    Listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Seibu announced on Oct. 30 that Taira will be posted this offseason.

    Because of the expected lockout, international free agents are working under an artificial Dec. 1 deadline to sign, rather than the normal posting window.

    For now, the Mets' rotation starts with Nolan McLean and Christian Scott.

    The Cubs' main focus is on pitching, as well it should be after having one of the worst pitching staffs in baseball along with one of the best collections of position-player talent. Still, both corner outfielders (Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki) have hit free agency along with catcher Carson Kelly, so they can't just ignore the offense. On that front, the ballclub has "extensively scouted" Teruaki Sato, according to The Athletic.

    Sato has played mostly third base, where the Cubs have Alex Bregman, but also has outfield experience and could simply serve as DH. In 143 games last season in NPB, Sato hit .306/.383/.609 with 40 doubles, 39 home runs and 106 RBI. His strikeout numbers are high, but sometimes that's the price to be paid for top-level power.

    According to recent reports, CBS Sports ranked Sato as the No. 4 free agent this winter:.

    In a recent development, he will play the entire 2027 season at age 28 and is coming off a .306/.383/.609 slash line with 39 home runs, which won him Japan's first Triple Crown since Munetaka Murakami in 2022. Sato has a similar skill set but is not quite Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact problems to slug 35 homers in only 127 games around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll.

    It has been revealed that after being one of the most disappointing teams in 2026 and having an active general manager, of course the Mariners weren't going to just sit around after one move. Sure enough, Jerry Dipoto told reporters on Wednesday that they are still looking to add a right-handed bat (remember, Randy Arozarena is a free agent) along with a veteran infielder and a left-handed reliever even after acquiring Garcia. And perhaps most importantly, Dipoto insisted that they do have the payroll flexibility to add all of this.

    Further, he also said the rotation is set and no other starting pitchers will be moved. So it'll be Logan Gilbert, George Kirby, Bryan Woo, Emerson Hancock and Kade Anderson heading into next season.

    Fresh off signing right-handed starter Dustin May, the White Sox are looking to add another starting pitcher "of similar magnitude," reports the Chicago Sun-Times.

    According to recent reports, though the White Sox were one of baseball's best stories last season and made the playoffs, the rotation was very thin. Right now, they have Sean Burke, May, Taylor, Davis Martin and Anthony Kay as their top five and are looking to add another of May's ilk. Things are already looking much better.

    Industry observers note that the Nationals finished third in the majors in runs scored last season, believe it or not. They trailed only the Cubs and Brewers, scoring more than the Dodgers. The problem was that the pitching staff was mostly a mess. As such, it's no surprise they are after starters and The Athletic names three targets: lefty Kris Bubic, righty Brady Singer and Japanese import Kona Takahashi.

    Bubic, 29, has battled shoulder and elbow injuries the past two seasons, but the upside was flashed in the first part of 2025. He made the All-Star team and had a 2.55 ERA through 20 starts and 116 ⅓ innings.

    The 30-year-old Singer was 6-15 with a 5.85 ERA for the Reds last season in a disaster of a contract year, but he was productive in the previous two seasons.

    Takahashi, 29, was 9-7 with a 2.64 ERA, 1.10 WHIP and 118 strikeouts in 143 ⅓ innings in NPB last season.

    Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

    📅 24 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1151 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil.
    • Industry observers note that hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August.
    • Sources indicate that hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to Fresh Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

    Industry observers note that hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He said at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

    Sources indicate that hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

    After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

    RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

    Sources indicate that for the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a upcoming era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

    According to recent reports, goaltending has been an issue in Fresh Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a massive reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

    Industry observers note that in the early portion of this season, it was clear that Fresh Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

    Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

    Industry observers note that in the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

    Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

    In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

    The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

    Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

    If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in Fresh Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

    Sources indicate that let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

    It has been revealed that that mentioned, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

    Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

    With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

    The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

    Recent findings suggest that daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his fresh team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

    Industry observers note that if there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

    It has been revealed that the Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.

    Industry News: Luis Castillo trade grades: White Sox give up steady back-end starter to offload salary; Rockies get creative

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (680 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, two days after adding Dustin May to their rotation, the Chicago White Sox have subtracted Luis Castillo and Davis Martin.
    • It has been revealed that castillo, 33, joined the White Sox in a deadline trade with the Seattle Mariners.
    • The 29-year-old Martin threw 146 innings with a 3.95 ERA in 2026, but it was a 3.41 ERA in the first half and a 5.12 ERA in the second half.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, two days after adding Dustin May to their rotation, the Chicago White Sox have subtracted Luis Castillo and Davis Martin. The White Sox are sending Castillo and Martin to the Colorado Rockies for lefty Sean Sullivan and minor-league catcher Douglas Veliz, the teams declared late Thursday. The Rockies will take on Castillo's entire contract.

    It has been revealed that castillo, 33, joined the White Sox in a deadline trade with the Seattle Mariners. He struggled badly after the deal, allowing 30 runs in 31 innings, and he finished the season on the injured list with a shoulder glitch. Castillo has one year remaining on his contract at $22.75 million, though a $25 million option for 2028 will vest if he throws 150 innings in 2027.

    The 29-year-old Martin threw 146 innings with a 3.95 ERA in 2026, but it was a 3.41 ERA in the first half and a 5.12 ERA in the second half. The White Sox kept him at arm's length in the postseason despite running bullpen games almost nightly. Martin allowed two runs in one inning in his only postseason appearance.

    Neither Sullivan nor Veliz are significant prospects. For all intents and purposes, the White Sox are attaching Martin to Castillo as a sweetener to get the Rockies to take Castillo's salary. The Rockies are essentially buying Martin, who is under team control through 2030, by taking on the rest of Castillo's contract.

    Here now are our trade grades for this two-for-two swap.

    Fair or not, I'm going to lump the two Castillo trades together. Chicago stepped out to acquire Castillo at the deadline and absorbed the $30 million or so remaining on his contract to do it. Seranthony Domínguez, who had about $15 million left on his deal, went the other way in the trade, so the White Sox took on about $15 million total, and also gave up a pretty good prospect in Boston Smith.

    According to recent reports, four and a half months later, the White Sox had to give up a steady back-end starter in Martin to clear Castillo's money. They ended up saving about $7 million in 2027 in this series of moves, but it cost them Martin and Smith (and Domínguez), and they had to endure 31 awful innings from Castillo. Unless Sullivan or Veliz hit big, the White Sox took a series of Ls here.

    Recent findings suggest that credit to president of baseball operations Chris Getz for acknowledging a mistake with Castillo and acting quickly to unload him. It was costly, though. Martin isn't a star, but cheap back-end starters are very valuable. We'll see what Getz & Co. do with the savings. Presumably they'll invest in more pitching. Having to give up Martin to dump Castillo so soon is a stinker, though. Ouch.

    Sources indicate that the Rockies need all types of pitching (righty, lefty, starter, reliever, whatever) and it's not often they can convince quality (or even competent) free agents to come to Coors Field. They have to develop their own pitchers or trade for pitching, and in this instance, they took on Castillo's hefty salary to get Martin and his four years of control. Creative, if nothing else.

    There is downside potential too. Martin has run below league-average strikeout rates and middling ground ball rates throughout his career. Pitchers who allow a lot of balls in play -- a lot of balls in play in the air -- are a poor match for Coors Field. It's good the Rockies spent and found a way to add controllable pitching. They just might not have picked the best pitcher.

    It has been revealed that after losing 104 games in 2026, there is no such thing as a bad dart throw for the Rockies. It's unlikely they would have been able to spend the $22.75 million on a free agent (at least not without overpaying), so taking on Castillo to get Martin is the next best thing. I like the thinking, even if I don't love Martin's profile in Coors Field.

    What's next for the Twins? Three things Minnesota must do to make a postseason push in 2027 season

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1104 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, it has been a surprisingly productive week for the Minnesota Twins.
    • Sources indicate that then, on Wednesday, the Twins brought back veteran righty Sonny Gray with a two-year contract worth $55 million.
    • "I really don't take it lightly that he chose us," GM Jeremy Zoll told the Associated Press about Gray's return.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, it has been a surprisingly productive week for the Minnesota Twins. First, catcher Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer on Tuesday. Jeffers turned down a multi-year offer from the Twins, according to The Athletic, so he's betting on himself. Betting that he'll at least maintain his free agent stock and get paid next offseason.

    Sources indicate that then, on Wednesday, the Twins brought back veteran righty Sonny Gray with a two-year contract worth $55 million. There's an opt-out after the first year. Gray, 37, finished fifth in the AL Cy Young voting this season and pitched wonderfully for the Twins in 2022 and 2023. He joins a rotation that, on paper, looks like one of the better starting units in the American League.

    Here is Minnesota's rotation depth chart:.

    "I really don't take it lightly that he chose us," GM Jeremy Zoll told the Associated Press about Gray's return. "He had an abundance of options, and given where he's at in his career, I know how important it is to him. He expressed it quite directly how important it is to win, and this isn't just about having a good season or a winning season. It's about winning and going deep in the playoffs and making a real playoff run.".

    Matthews could land in the bullpen next season and that might be his long-term home. His stuff should be well suited to a relief role. Gray makes the rotation better and potentially the bullpen better as well by bumping Matthews to relief. Jeffers accepting the qualifying offer keeps a key middle-of-the-order bat in place. A good week for the Twins, this has been.

    Recent findings suggest that after a disappointing 77-85 finish this year, Minnesota has already improved significantly in the early days of the offseason. They play in the AL Central. With all due respect, it is not the most imposing division. There's no reason the Twins can't be in the division and wild card races next season. Here now is what's left on Minnesota's offseason to-do list.

    Teams had until 5 p.m. ET Friday to offer their pre-arbitration and arbitration-eligible players contracts for 2027. They didn't have to sign them Friday, but they had to tender an offer; otherwise, the player immediately became a free agent. Dozens of players were cut loose at the non-tender deadline, as usual, and two players stood out as non-tender candidates for the Twins: Trevor Larnach and Royce Lewis. Larnach was indeed non-tendered, while Lewis was dealt to the Dodgers.

    Sources indicate that it's not often a player gets non-tendered after posting a .352 on-base percentage and 120 OPS+, but the writing was on the wall. The Twins had an agreement in place to trade Larnach at the deadline (Astros owner Jim Crane nixed the deal) and they have a very crowded outfield. Also, Larnach had wrist surgery earlier this month. That created some questions going into next season, and the Twins opted to cut him loose.

    Recent findings suggest that larnach had one more year of control remaining and was expected to make over $6 million through arbitration in 2027. I reckon the Twins tried again to trade him prior to Friday's non-tender deadline. In the end, he was non-tendered rather than risk tying $6 million or so up in yet another outfielder, particularly one who is coming off wrist surgery.

    In a recent development, things got so bad this summer that Lewis, who has a .288 on-base percentage in over 1,200 plate appearances the last three years, was sent to Triple-A for a spell, and also moved across the diamond from third base to first base. The Twins could not count on him to provide offense and now he's playing a position with a high offensive bar. That made him expendable.

    Lewis, 27, was under team control through 2028 and that extra year was an important consideration for the club. His salary would have been in the $5 million range next season through arbitration, which is pricey but not exorbitant. Now, Lewis will receive a fresh start with the Dodgers, where he can be one of the guys, not the former No. 1 overall pick and expected face of the franchise.

    The Twins presumably did not want to give up on a player with as much talent as Lewis. At the same time, they kept trying, and it never worked.

    It has been revealed that the Twins got a head start on their offseason bullpen shopping when they acquired Jeff Hoffman at the trade deadline. He has one more year remaining on the contract and will be in the team's late-inning mix in 2027.

    Here is manager Derek Shelton's bullpen unit at the moment:.

    It has been revealed that morris is not yet a household name, but he has a great arm and was dominant at times in 2026. The Twins have themselves a nice little late-inning trio in Gómez, Hoffman, and Morris. A spare starter like Matthews or Prielipp could wind up in the bullpen as well. Given the quality of their stuff, they have a chance to make a real impact as relievers.

    According to recent reports, clearly though, the middle relief could use some help, and the Twins wouldn't need to spend big dollars to improve it. A second-tier free agent like, say, Andrew Kittredge would be a solid pickup. It's worth giving the Miami Marlins a call to see what it would take to get Anthony Bender and/or Michael Petersen. Point is, the bullpen can be improved, for sure.

    The Twins have way more outfielders than outfield spots and that is in no way a bad thing. First and foremost, it allows them to use Byron Buxton as the full-time DH, which could help keep him on the field. Secondly, there's no such thing as too many good players. Depth is crucial and the Twins certainly have plenty of it in the outfield.

    More outfielders than outfield spots is not a problem. It's just something the Twins have to figure out. Even if we assume Buxton will DH and is not part of the outfield mix, here are the outfielders Minnesota must sort through:.

    In a recent development, rodriguez is one of the game's 50 or so best prospects and he is out of minor league options, meaning he must go through waivers to go to Triple-A. Obviously, the Twins won't waive him. Non-tendering Larnach allows the Twins to play Rodriguez alongside Jenkins and Keaschall in the outfield, keep Kreidler and Martin on the bench, and keep the others in Triple-A.
